faq.q: How can I check a jewelry photo before publishing?
faq.a: Put the download next to the shot you took and read the engraving. A prong that moved means that file stays off the site. On a large upload, the API can hold back frames that fail the same look.

faq.q: Can I try the API on one piece before the whole catalog?
faq.a: Yes. Send one earring, not the whole tray, and read that result before the catalog run.

faq.q: What should the source photo include?
faq.a: A sharp frame of the complete piece on a plain surface, with the chain, clasp, stones, and mount visible.

faq.q: Can I show how a necklace sits?
faq.a: Yes. Choose a view at the neck and keep the chain in the photo. Put the measured length and the material in the listing text.
Necklaces, earrings, rings, bracelets, and cufflinks, when your photo shows their shape and surface. If a detail is cut off in the source, the new photo can miss it too.

faq.q: How do I keep a stone or clasp faithful?
faq.a: Compare the download with your original at full size. Keep a version whose stone, mount, clasp, and color still match. Do not keep a photo that invents a claw or shifts the metal.

faq.q: Can I clear the background and set the light?
faq.a: Yes. The grey cloth can go, and a shadow can sit under the piece so the metal stays easy to read.

faq.q: Do I need to book a jewelry model?
faq.a: No. A worn picture is built from your piece photo. Ask for a neck on a pendant, and a hand on a ring. The person you see is an AI model.

faq.q: What does a jewelry photo cost?
faq.a: Each photo costs 24 credits. Starter is $24.50 a month with 200 credits, Pro is $35 with 300, and Premium is $63 with 600. You see the cost before you start. A failed render returns the credits. The download has no watermark.

faq.q: What if I want a scene with no person?
faq.a: Use a table scene when size on a body is not the point. Photos with no person are on the [lifestyle product photos](page:lifestyle-photos) page.

steps.prompt: Show an adult wearing the silver necklace at the collarbone, with a light touch on the chain so the size is easy to judge. Keep the pendant and chain visible, in soft window light.

definition.title: Realistic Jewelry Photos Need a Careful Edit
paras: A clasp, a link, or a stone has to stay recognizable, and the shot you already have is the start. Clear the cloth, keep the metal color, and put one shadow under the piece. A fine chain still needs that care.
A neck view shows how far a pendant drops. A plain desk works when the listing does not need a person for scale. The API can run the next photo in that same look.

items.d: One sharp photo, clasp included, is enough to see how the edit treats the piece.
Clear the cloth on that single photo and the links come out separate, still matching the piece you shot.
You see the 24 credits before a photo runs, and a failed run sends those credits back.

trust.lead: Retouch bills drop, the email matches the site, and the piece on both still looks like your photo.

items.d: A full tray of studs can start from photos you already shot. You spend 24 credits a photo instead of mailing each stud out for a hand cutout.
The bangle on the product page and the bangle in the newsletter can share one background. The gold does not go warm in one place and cold in the other.
You choose the file that goes up, and the next shots can use that same look.

reasons.h2: Fine Pieces Without a Hand Retouch
reasons.lead: Keep the links, keep the metal color, and run the next photo through that same edit.

items.d: Each link stays separate when the grey cloth goes, and the metal color stays with the photo you took. A polished cuff can use the same edit.
The gold stays the color you shot, on an AI actor or on a styled table, and the shimmer stays with the piece.
The next photo can use the square you chose, with a shadow sitting under the piece rather than floating beside it. Your catalog can hand the next SKU to the API.

benefits.t: Clear the Table and the Props
benefits.d: Paper tags and pin heads come off a tangled charm bracelet first. A mirror-finish band can leave the grey cloth in that same edit, and the stand comes off too.
A soft shadow sits under the metal so a diamond table or a platinum edge stays readable. The gold keeps the color from your photo.
On an old locket, the engraving stays the shape you photographed while the area around the piece changes.
A size-5 ring and a size-9 ring sit on the same point of the square. A long necklace can take a taller crop when it needs the length, and the ring row keeps its own square.
A pendant's length is easy to judge at the collarbone on an AI actor, and you do not book a model for that shot. A ring can use a hand for scale.
When one brooch looks right, that crop can run across the whole tray. The API can start the next piece from your catalog.

benefits_h2: Jewelry Edits for the Whole Tray
benefits_lead: Clear the cloth, set one shadow, and run that crop across the tray so the piece still looks like the photo you took.

closing.h2: Hold a Quality Bar on Every Photo
